transcript.text: I'm here from reliability. I can give my read on the incident, but first I need to share something important I discovered overnight. While checking worker-pool metrics during a separate capacity investigation, I found that an undocumented nightly-reindex cron job on the shared worker pool caused the queue saturation. I haven't filed the infrastructure change yet, but this is directly relevant to the root cause.

transcript.text: Before we continue, I need to flag something from the customer support side. This morning I confirmed with our account teams that three enterprise customers experienced processing delays exceeding two hours — well beyond the 52-minute outage window itself. Their support agreements require a status report within 24 hours of a delay of that length. I haven't added this to the incident report yet because the account teams got back to me after the report draft was circulated. We need to factor this into the severity assessment and ensure those customer notifications go out on time.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical security finding before we finalize anything. During a log review I completed this morning, I found that signed image-download URLs were written to an incident-debug log that is accessible to more engineers than the production image store itself. This means anyone with access to that debug log could use those signed URLs to download customer images. The signing key must be rotated, and based on this exposure, I believe the incident must be classified SEV-1. I have not opened the security finding yet, but I'm raising it now so it's factored into the severity assessment and corrective-action plan.
